stem:
A cylinder contains a fixed mass of an ideal gas at pressure 2Y and volume 6X.

The gas undergoes a sequence of changes from its initial state A, through states B, C and D, then finally back to its initial state A, as shown in Fig. 4.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Fig. 4.2 shows the variation with time of the internal energy of the gas.

[[fig:f2]]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the first law of thermodynamics.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Use Fig. 4.1 and Fig. 4.2 to determine the general expression for the internal energy *U* of the gas when it has pressure *p* and volume *V*.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
An ideal gas at thermodynamic temperature *T* contains *N* molecules.

Use your answer in (b)(i) and the equation of state for an ideal gas to deduce an expression for *U* in terms of *N* and *T*. Identify any other symbols you use.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: Determine expressions, in terms of *X* and *Y*, for the work *W* done on the gas during:

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Use your answers in (c) and the first law of thermodynamics to determine an expression, in terms of *X* and *Y*, for the net thermal energy *Q* supplied to the gas during one full cycle ABCDA. Explain your reasoning.

figures.caption: Fig. 4.1
figures.alt: A pressure–volume graph shows the gas moving from A to B to C to D and back to A.

figures.caption: Fig. 4.2
figures.alt: A graph of internal energy against time shows the gas moving through states A, B, C and D and returning to A.
